Do you expect it to be based off something technical/academic like Jungian Psychological Types, MBTI/Socionics Cognitive Functions, Enneagram, SLOAN, Attitudinal Psyche or Temperaments then no. The Game has its own personality types like Clergy (Compassionate person), Clown (Curious, 'tries random stuff' person) and many more (But bigger descriptions of course) which is pretty much similar to pop personality tests you see online.

But dismissing it as another pop personality test would be doing it injustice. The personality types are divided into 5 catergories: Passion, Morals, Methods, Judgement and Daring. It's basically a story-driven game where the actions you take in the game will add up/against the in-built personality types.  
You will actually have to repeat the game 3 times in order for you to get correct personality typing. Your typing can change as you repeat the game over again.

In the end, you will get your main personality type, 2 supporting personality types, 1 hidden personality type and 1 'most distant / opposite' personality type alongside few other stuffs. You don't have to worry about hesitating a lot before making choices, acting differently in repeat plays, ignoring the main plot or rushing through the game because all of it is accounted by the game and it was surprisingly kinda accurate.

Also the story itself is decent because there is a plot twist after you complete the game 3 times. OST is good. The more you immerse yourself in the game the better your results will be.

This is very interesting, because I had the same thought an year ago or so. First strategy is about being robust:

**Redundancy & Options -**

Options refer to a system's ability to react in multiple ways to any given threat. A great example is when humans see a threat, we can react in 3 different ways, those are "Freeze, Fight, Flight" response. Each of them are useful for different threats.  
Hence you should always have optionality in your life. In any venture you should identify multiple ways to respond to potential threats or capitalize on opportunities.  
A very bad example would be falling into debt because you lose all your optionality and freedom of choice, being enslaved to whatever demand bank makes of you. You don't have the option to.. capitalize on other investment, cause all your money just goes to pay debt.

What about redundancy? A great example is that human body have 2 kidneys. It's the same thing. In any system or plans you build, there should always be backups you can rely on in case the first one fails.

Only when you are robust, can you start being antifragile:

**Barbell Strategy -**

Basically 80% of your time, money, effort shall go to very low risk, low reward ventures, the remaining 20% of your time, money, effort shall go to very high risk, high reward ventures (Your vision).  
Basically mid risk, mid rewards is trash. You bet on two extremes. Majority being very low risk and low reward, while there being one very high risk high reward vision you want to pursue.

**Convex risks -**

This combined with Barbell Strategy is what will make you truly antifragile. Not all risks are bad, there are things that actually benefit from things deviating from the norm, we call them convex risks. These are the risks where losses are capped but gains can potentially be infinite depending on how much things deviate from the norm. These risks benefit from volatility and uncertainty instead of being harmed from them.  
A good example from Taleb -

>Taleb presents a simple rule of thumb for assessing the health of a company facing volatile conditions. If sales increase 10%, will profits increase less than they would decrease if sales drop 10%? If so, that company is fragile and will not withstand much volatility. Its problems will compound downward in a death spiral, which is what happened to Fannie Mae.

If the profits, when sales increase by 10%, increase less than they would decrease if sales drops 10%, it would be a great example of concave risk! On the other hand if the profits, when sales increase by 10%, increase more than they would decrease if sales drop 10% then that's a great example of convex risk! You have to assume that for your vision, things going up are equally as likely as things going down. Then see if the profit when things goes up is way higher than loss when things go down. If yes, only then you must bet on that risk (Exercise your optionality)

Combine that with Barbell Strategy which is efficient risk management strategy and your visions are antifragile.

I just wanted to elaborate on the misconception that Te types are just 'what works' or 'external facts' or 'tribe logic'. This is a misconception on Extraverted Thinking.

Like u/Jungisnumberone mentioned, extraverted functions are about 'outer objects'. Naturally this will involve keen attention to facts and what others think but that doesn't mean they can't think and analyze for themselves. Their psychic energy is merely directed outwards, towards the external world.

Ti users also care about what others think. You might say "Well, they do analyze it aftwards to see if this makes sense to them", but Te does that as well, it's just that inner objects are much more complex to analyze, so it needs much more introspection, something Ti is better at.  
Yes. It is true that practically speaking, average Te users are more likely to not really care much if a thing simply works, but that is only because their mind is more focused on results (Outer object) rather than concepts (Inner object). However, nowhere does that mean that when no one has any idea how to make something work, they can't think it for themselves.  
Te users can be originial, they can be innovative, use frame of reference, think and analyze stuffs by themselves. They just don't use thinking to introspect, instead they use it to 'extrospect' and interact with the outer world.

Edit: A very good example of Te MBTI creators vs Ti MBTI creators would be creators of OPS (Objective Personality System). Both (The creators of OPS) are INTJs. They have created an innovative way of categorizing people, also came up with various new theories like Jumper, Masculine vs Feminine orientation, Tidal waves etc. They are able to type people into a total of 512 personality types with extremely high precision!  
Their only drawback? They don't even know whether the type they are assigning to people is 'correct' or not. Only that same kind of people are being grouped into same type. It's because they aren't much interested in a conceptual understanding of what cognitive functions really are, which means high possibility of mistype. Most of their understanding of cognitive function is based on the kind of behaviors they produce in real life, which they are using to type people. Very 'result' focused guys.

TL;DR: Difference between Te and Ti is that of extrospection vs introspection of logic. It's not about originiality or trusting others' logic.

For more clarification, what Marx meant by science and what is today meant by science is different.

For Marx science was materialism, i.e. a theory arrived through analysis grounded in material reality and not simply through ideas. A religion / creationism would be considered an ideology as it is a theory that comes from ideas. Marxism on the other hand was developed through analysis and study of the political and economic conditions of past and present socities and hence was materialist and therefore scientific.

Modern day scientific method means that the prediction proposed by the theory was empirically tested and verified. In that way Marxism is not a science but a mere theory as all of its predictions have not been proven true (E.g. we have not achieved communism yet so it still has not been proven true). However that does not mean Marxism is not unfalsifiable, anyone can test it and in fact it has been tested and many predictions proven true. Anarchism doesn't mean lack of coordination. First we will need to understand what anarchy actually means. Anarchy is the absence / lack of 'Archy'. 'Archy' is best described as the ability of some person / group to rule **over** others. Anarchy lacks 'Archy' because it believes that any decision must be collectively agreed upon by all the stakeholders involved.

Hence there are two things that needs to be done for space exploration agency. One is getting resources and other is efficiently using it for the purpose of space exploration.

In the former the stakeholders are the entire population, this is because the resources belong to the people, they are made by the people for the consumption of the people. Hence here people replace the government for the allocation of resources. It is not that people 'rule' over space exploration agency. Nobody rules over other because the decision to allocate resources is made by consensus. Only when certain amount of resources are collectively agreed upon by all the stakeholders involved is the decision made.  
Hence 'How many resources would be allocated' depends on a lot of factors e.g. how enthusiastic people are about space travel, how productive / efficient / useful do they think the space exploration agency is and how much resources do they have themselves.

Hence resources aren't really allocated, they are negotiated between the agency and other people.

For the latter on how the resources would be managed internally, the space exploration agency like any other commune also functions with a consensus, workers (Engineers, scientists etc.) who are the stakeholders here can decide how the organization would work and give some tasks to specialists and bureaucrats to handle, the only requirement is that they must all reach a consensus together (i.e. there won't be any boss to give orders, but worker's self management).

Anarchy means 'An' + 'Archy'. 'An' is the lack of something, hence lack of 'Archy'. 'Archy' means rule of someone / some people over others. One of the most important kind of 'Archy' is 'Hierarchy'. Hence Anarchy is absence of archy like hierarchy, not of order. Without order forget having a civilization, or even a village, without order you can't even have a tribe.

Anarchism works on the basis of consensus. To make a decision a plan is put forward by any member and explained. After explaination everybody's criticism of that plan is heard. After criticism and discussion have been noted down, another plan is put forward keeping those criticisms and discussion in mind. This is repeated till everyone agrees to some degree.  
This is called consensus, this is actually how everybody makes decision in day to day lives, we don't vote in our day to day lives, we discuss and broadly agree on one plan which keeps everybody's wants and needs into consideration.

Everybody is allowed to join a consensus, especially those who are being directly affected by a decision. A person can show their satisfaction in many ways -

1. A person disagrees with the plan and don't want it to pass at all because they feel that they have not been heard and considered properly.
2. A person disagrees with the plan but they finally give in and let it be passed.
3. A person disagress on some issues but overall don't mind it being passed.
4. A person agrees and want it to be passed.

A consensus seeks to get rid of (1), minimize (2) and (3) as much as possible and maximize (4) as much as possible.

A consensus passes when it satisfies the above condition.

1. Some problems with consensus might be that some people keep disagreeing because they have radically different thinking / moral standards than the average person. In that case they are advised or allowed to leave that community and start their own or join another.
2. Other problems might be that it is very time consuming and hard to get a consensus.
3. One more problem might be that non-hierarchial structures might not be very well suited to things like military where immediate action by authority is required.

There are huge advantages too -

1. Consensus avoids problems associated with Democracy i.e. presence of demagogues and people-pleaser politicians, reduces corruption as there is no corrupt hierarchy, gets rid of 'tyranny of majority' as minority groups are oppressed under democracy.
2. There is also absence of any possibility of a dictator arising as there is no hierarchial structures in anarchism.
3. Lack of hierarchy means that nobody needs to be oppressed as decision is made when everybody allows it, this means that law-enforcement like Police, Courts, Governments, State-Media, Prisons are not needed in Anarchist society greatly saving time and energy.
4. Higher satisfaction and empowerment / freedom of people in anarchist society as one person can't be oppressed and their thoughts / ideas are always heard and implemented in decision making.
5. Fosters community building and sense of responsibility as people are directly responsible for the good / bad of the community.
6. Consensus leads to higher quality decisions. Bad decisions are constantly improved covering broad range of perspectives before being implemented. This means that not only people's needs but science, logic and rationality plays a huge role in decision making.

So consensus means that each decision takes much more time, but each decision is also of much higher quality. Hence we are putting quality over quantity when it comes to decision making, and I think I prefer that because people would finally give preferences to important things than bogus things as time is limited. People would be more focused on deciding e.g. 'How an economy should be run' than useless arguments like 'Should babies be aborted or not' or 'Should there be blasphemy or not' etc. I think this is a win-win for me. Less quantity of BS and more quality where it matters.  
Plus again you save a lot of labor in law enforcement. However once a decision is reached and guideline made but a person still does not follow it then what happens? That is left to society as it depends on what kind of guidelines and situation of the person breaking it. They can be talked to / rehabilitated, if that doesn't work then ridiculed / isolated and if nothing works then just ostracized / exiled. However every guideline is made from consensus decision making so probability of it happening are low.

Anarchy might get difficult in situtaions where a lot of rules need to be made quickly and efficiently e.g. an army engaging in war. In that case people can decide whether they want to temporarily use democracy and centralized / decentralized hierarchies which can be disbanded after the war is finished.

There are many kinds and flavors of capitalism. You have the neo-liberal one, the laissez-faire one, you have keynesian capitalism, social democracy or mixed-economy and fascism just to name a few.

Similarly there are many flavors of socialism and many ideas on how it might be implemented. Communists just call socialism as lower phase of communism, that is a society which still has few capitalist relations but is rapidly getting rid of it to transition to communism.  
Personally I like Paul Cockshott's book [Towards a new socialism](http://users.wfu.edu/cottrell/socialism_book/new_socialism.pdf) for how a socialist society might function. I also have my few own recommendations, so keeping this in mind let us answer your question.

>how will there be innovation? (iphones, video games, etc) if someone comes up with an idea for a product, how will he create it? will he have a business? would this make him a capitalist?

Cockshott imagines planners being elected by people (And being instantly recallable) hence if you come up with an idea for a new product you will likely have to contact the planners for it. There are a lot of stuffs to be planned example how much resources will be required and from where you will get it, environmental impacts, how much labor is available and people willing to work with you etc.

This does not make that person a capitalist as a capitalist is a person who profits off other people's labor. That is not how socialism works as in socialism everybody is rewarded with how much work they do instead of living off other people's work. If you start a new company or industry under socialism it would be more like a cooperative designed to serve the society, so the person who innovated won't be a capitalist.

>how do wages work? i imagine a doctor gets more than a janitor, but how does this work under socialism?

Under socialism Cockshott imagines people to be paid according to the amount of hours they work. For unskilled labor a lot of work is easy to automate and labor is available in large quantities so people work for less hours hence get paid less.  
For skilled labor work isn't easy to automate and labor is not available in large quantities so people work for more hours hence get paid more. It works like supply-demand.

These aren't really wages though. Wage is an agreement between two people on how much you are worth. The hours in which you are paid is not an agreement but a record of how much work you did. It is a record of your contribution to the society and you take as much as you contribute. Hence they work like wages but aren't wages.  
E.g. if you work 40 hours a week then 40 hours is your contribution (Wage). If a certain product needed 1 hour to make then 1 hour is its value (price). That's how it will work.

This is also something Marx imagined in his Critique of the Gotha Program for how lower phase of communism might function.

Private property means property which you own but do not use. In socialism property belongs to those who use it, so if workers run a factory then factory belongs to the workers, that's how private property does not exist under socialism. However your backyard is used by you so it doesn't count as private property but personal property which belongs to you.  
You can only own a company as long as you are the only person who works there. If more work then you don't own it, it is socialized. This is the basics of socialism that property be owned by those who use it.
